title.narrative: CLACSO: Plattformar för social dialog Latinamerika
CLACSO: Social Dialogue Platforms Latin America

description.narrative:
Denna insats avser programstöd till Latin American Council of Social Sciences (CLACSO), en internationell icke-statlig institution, associerad med Unesco, som inrättades 1967. Det samlar för närvarande 836 forsknings- och forskarutbildningscentra inom samhällsvetenskap och humaniora i 55 länder i Latinamerika och andra världsdelar.
Sida kommer att stödja programmet Social Sciences in the face of inequality in Latin America and the Caribbean: Social Dialogue Platforms, andel Programmets huvudsakliga mål är att producera evidensbaserad, kritisk och kontextrelevant kunskap i syfte att påverka utformningen av politik, allmän opinion och bidra till positiva förändringar av levnadsvillkoren för de mest fattiga, förtryckta och diskriminerade befolkningsgrupperna i Latinamerika och Karibien.
För att uppnå detta utvecklas sex s.k plattformar för social dialog på regional nivå för att samordna och främja utbyten mellan olika aktörer inom den akademiska världen, det civila samhället och aktörer inom den offentliga politiken i syfte att:
1. På regional nivå gemensamt producera evidensbaserad och jämförande kunskap baserad på samverkan inom nätverk, rörelser, institutioner och samhällen.
2. Utveckla färdigheter och kompetenser för att öka kapaciteten för social aktivism, främja forskning samt kritisk och kontextrelevant kunskap.
3. Främja och intensifiera utbyte mellan sociala rörelser, akademiker och företrädare för offentlig politik för att utveckla gemensamma handlingsprogram.
4. Utveckla kommunikations- och påverkanskampanjer utformade för att mobilisera och influera den allmänna opinionen, med tonvikt på att synliggöra situationen för marginaliserade och utsatta grupper.
För varje plattform för social dialog har definierats ett tematiskt mål: 1. Ojämlikhet och fattigdom 2. Demokrati, mänskliga rättigheter och fred 3. Sociala rörelser och aktivism 4. Rättigheter, våld och jämställdhet 5. Miljö, klimatförändringar och social utveckling 6. Migration och mänsklig rörlighet
Detta program förväntas bidra till sektorn för mänskliga rättigheter, eftersom det fördjupar den akademiska friheten och rätten till utbildning.

This contribution is a program support for the Latin American Council of Social Sciences (CLACSO), an international non-governmental institution, associated with UNESCO and created in 1967. It currently brings together 836 research and postgraduate centers in the field of social sciences and humanities in 55 countries in Latin America and other continents.
Sida will support the Social Sciences in the face of inequality in Latin America and the Caribbean: Social Dialogue Platforms program, which main objective of achieving the production of evidence-based, critical and situated knowledge with a high impact on the definition of policies, the formation of public opinion and the positive transformation of the living conditions of the most impoverished, oppressed and discriminated populations of Latin America & the Caribbean.
To this end, six (6) Social Dialogue Platforms (SDP) will be developed in the regional level, to articulate and promote multi-stakeholder exchanges between the academic community, civil society organizations and public policies practitioners in order to:
1. Co-produce evidence-based knowledge in a comparative perspective and regional scale, based on the articulation of networks, movements, institutions, and communities.
2. Develop skills and competences to enhance the capacities of social activism, promote research and the generation of critical and situated knowledge.
3. Promote and densify the exchanges between social movements, academics, and public policy practitioners to develop joint action programs.
4. Develop communication and advocacy campaigns, designed to mobilize, and impact public opinion, with emphasis on making visible the situations of excluded and vulnerable groups.
Each of the projected six (6) Social Dialogue Platforms will comprise a thematic objective: 1. Inequalities and poverty 2. Democracy, human rights, and peace 3. Social movements and activism 4. Rights, violence, and gender equality 5. Environment, climate change and social development 6. Migration and human mobility
This program is expected to make a contribution to the Human Rights sector, as it deepens academic freedom and the right to education.

The general objective of the Project Social Sciences in the face of inequality in Latin America and the Caribbean: Social Dialogue Platforms is the production of evidence-based, critical, and situated knowledge with a high impact on the definition of policies, the formation of public opinion and the positive transformation of the living conditions of the most impoverished, oppressed, and discriminated populations in the region.
To this end, a device called Social Dialogue Platforms will be implemented, a collaborative and multi-stakeholder workspace designed to promote exchanges between the academic community, civil society organizations and public policies practitioners, have a concrete impact in pressing thematic issues for Latin America & the Caribbean and contribute to the construction of common regional agendas that have a demonstrable impact on improving the life of the most neglected sectors of society and of those who suffer different forms of oppression.
The Social Dialogue Platforms have four (4) main purposes: 1. Co-produce evidence-based knowledge in a comparative perspective and regional scale, based on the articulation of networks, movements, institutions, and communities. 2. Develop skills and competences to enhance the capacities of social activism, promote research and the generation of critical and situated knowledge. 3. Promote and densify the exchanges between social movements, academics, and public policy practitioners to develop joint action programs. 4. Develop communication and advocacy campaigns, designed to mobilize, and impact public opinion, with emphasis on making visible the situations of excluded and vulnerable groups.

The expectation for Sida, for the first year of the project, indicated that efforts were going to be focused mainly to building the Social Dialogue Platforms (Social Dialogue Platforms website: https://www.clacso.org/plataformasparaeldialogosocial/), however CLACSO had an already strong structure that could be quickly transformed into more thematic platforms that increasingly are attracting a wide array of actors.
In 2022, CLACSO begun to develop a new way of working with the thematic platforms as umbrellas of the efforts they do in the different fields such as research (collective and individual thematic investigation participative action), publications (open and accessible to all the public), formation (education for a wider spectrum of actors, not necessarily academics) and communications (multiformat to create nontraditional products that could impact public opinion).
The new way of working indicates that those individual processes of research publications, formation and communications should have convergence moments, to increase the impact by gathering the actors involved, that now have become International Thematic Forums. This new way of working is still to be consolidated in a routine of activities arranged to have a wider impact, but it is model that clearly delivers impact across the four outcomes of the project: 1. Coproduce evidencebased knowledge on a regional scale and in the six thematic areas of common interest for Sida and CLACSO 2. Develop skills and competences for social activism tied to critical and situated knowledge of Latin America 3. Promote and densify the exchanges between the triangle of actors (academy, decision makers and activism) and 4. Develop communication and advocacy campaigns with impact that reaches the periphery of Latin America.
Regarding the Social Dialogue Platforms some hed a robust development in the first year, such as the Democracy, human rights, and peace (2), Social movements and activism (3), Rights, violence, and gender equality (4) and Environment, climate change and social development (5). Thus, a challenge is to balance the developments of the Migration and human mobility (6) and the Inequalities and poverty (1) platforms.
Furthermore, it is worth bringing up that CLACSO based on Sida program, was able to build two more Social Dialogue Platform (The right to education, public policy, and alternative pedagogy (7), as well as the Reconfiguration if work in the current world (8)), drawing from other sources of funding. This means that the project leveraged resources form other international cooperation actors, that are reinforcing the objective of the program and the sustainability of the activities in the longterm.
In general terms, in relation to the main objective of the project it could be assessed that the production of evidence-based, critical, and situated knowledge was accomplished beyond the planned indicators of success. One important aspect is that CLACSO is bringing these results into the periphery of Latin America decentralizing and democratizing knowledge. Nevertheless, what is still a challenge for CLACSO is how to increase the impact on the definition of policies, the formation of public opinion and, ultimately, the positive transformation of the living conditions of the most impoverished, oppressed, and discriminated populations of Latin America.
